goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_021) Identify and analyze five major causes of the Great Depression (1929-1933). For each cause, state the causal mechanism, name the primary economist(s) associated with that explanation, and identify one empirical objection.
ground_truth: 1. Banking panics and money supply contraction (Friedman and Schwartz, A Monetary History): bank failures caused M1 to fall 33%; objection: banks failed partly due to bad agricultural loans, not just panics. 2. Stock market crash (initial Keynesian account): asset wealth destruction reduced aggregate demand; objection: stock crash alone does not explain the depth or 3-year duration. 3. Smoot-Hawley tariffs (trade economists): 1930 tariffs triggered retaliatory trade restrictions, contracting world trade by 66%; objection: US exports were a small fraction of GDP, limiting direct impact. 4. Gold standard propagation (Eichengreen, Temin): fixed exchange rates forced deflationary adjustment globally; objection: not all gold standard countries suffered equally (France held gold longer). 5. Aggregate demand collapse (Keynes): self-reinforcing spending decline; objection: independent demand trigger is hard to identify separately from financial crisis.
